text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Radiation oncology consultation to review staging and discuss curative treatment options and short-term androgen deprivation
  • Staging for unfavorable intermediate-risk disease with PSMA PET/CT
  • Treatment chosen through shared decision-making: image-guided external beam radiotherapy to the prostate with six months of androgen deprivation (leuprolide, with bicalutamide for the first four weeks)
  • Androgen deprivation monitoring: testosterone, PSA, blood pressure, glucose and lipids, DXA at baseline and every one to two years, vitamin D and calcium, hot flashes, mood, and cognition
  • After radiotherapy: PSA every six months for five years, then yearly, with recurrence defined as a rise of 2 ng/mL above the nadir (Phoenix); urinary and bowel symptoms at every visit
  • Distress screening at each visit, physical activity, and a written survivorship care plan

resource.title: Nelson Mandela synthetic care plan
resource.description: Localized prostate cancer found by a rising PSA in a fit man of 82, on the NCCN prostate guideline, the AUA/ASTRO 1997 localized prostate cancer guideline, and the CMID prostate cancer monograph: risk grouping and staging (unfavorable intermediate risk, with PSMA PET); shared decision-making among observation, radiotherapy with short-term androgen deprivation, and surgery, with life expectancy and an earlier prostate operation weighed; six months of androgen deprivation with radiotherapy, and the monitoring it needs (testosterone, bone density and vitamin D, glucose and lipids, blood pressure, hot flashes, mood, and cognition); urinary and bowel effects of radiotherapy; and PSA surveillance after radiotherapy with the Phoenix definition of recurrence. His doctors' public account, a slight PSA rise on monitoring, a biopsy, hormone therapy, and a seven-week course of curative radiotherapy, frames the episode.
